research_question: Does a larger training set narrow the single-snapshot Transformer gap to matched logistic regression and delay the rise in development log loss?
sampling: Sort match IDs within each event, then use one NumPy default_rng stream per draw. Permute each event in the stated event order and take prefixes for each size. Use the same complete 32-match split for both draws.
training: Inherit the frozen 47-feature, FP32, AdamW, constant learning rate, 64-snapshot batch, and single-snapshot architecture from the matched epoch experiment. Fit the same median imputer and round-weighted scaler for both models within each fit subset. Keep one total weight per recorded round.
primary_comparison: Transformer epoch 1 minus logistic Log Loss within each draw and training size, then the 32-match gap minus the 16-match gap within each draw. Negative gap change indicates a narrower loss disadvantage when the 16-match gap is positive.
curve_policy: Plot both fit and development Log Loss after every epoch through epoch 20. Record the earliest development minimum and the epoch-20 loss minus that minimum as descriptions. Retain epoch 1 as the scoring comparison across all sizes and training seeds.
reuse: Reuse the exact 32-match epoch-1 weights and probabilities and the first 20 curve rows per training seed from the frozen development run. Fit one new matched logistic model on those 32 matches.
development_scope: The same 10 previously observed BLAST Bounty and Esports World Cup Mirage matches. All candidates and all contrasts use the identical 3,945 prediction ticks with equal total weight per round.
